proof_skeleton_nl: First reduce an arbitrary real x to its fractional part t = x - floor(x). By integer-shift invariance, f_n(x) = f_n(t), and the standard fractional-part identity gives 0 <= t < 1. For such a t, let m = floor(n*t). The floor-interval lemma places t in [m/n, (m+1)/n), and the interval comparison gives f_n(t) <= g_n(m). The discrete bottleneck lemma then yields g_n(m) <= H_n - 1, so every reduced t in [0,1) satisfies f_n(t) <= H_n - 1, hence every real x satisfies f_n(x) <= H_n - 1. On the top interval [1 - 1/n, 1), the explicit computation shows floor(k*t) = k - 1 for all 1 <= k <= n, so f_n(t) = H_n - 1; by periodicity this gives equality for every x whose fractional part lies in that interval. If the fractional part t is smaller than 1 - 1/n, then m = floor(n*t) cannot equal n - 1, so the equality case in the discrete lemma is impossible; this forces strict inequality f_n(x) < H_n - 1. Therefore the global maximizers are exactly the real numbers x whose fractional part x - floor(x) lies in [1 - 1/n, 1), equivalently x = z + t with z an integer and t in [1 - 1/n, 1), and the maximal value is H_n - 1.

steps.derives: For an arbitrary real x, let t = x - floor(x). Then 0 <= t < 1 and f_n(x) = f_n(t).
steps.trivial_justification: This combines the fractional-part decomposition with integer-shift invariance; it is not a single direct substitution.

steps.derives: If m = floor(n*t) for the reduced variable t from A1, then t lies in the interval [m/n, (m+1)/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the floor-interval characterization stated by the lemma.

steps.derives: For that interval index m, the reduced value f_n(t) is bounded above by g_n(m).
steps.trivial_justification: The lemma directly provides the interval-wise upper bound.

steps.derives: For every reduced t in [0,1), the value f_n(t) is at most H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: This uses the interval bound from A3 together with the discrete bound and transitivity of inequalities.

steps.derives: For every real x, the original expression f_n(x) is at most H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply A1 to replace x by its fractional part t and then use A4 for that reduced variable.

steps.derives: If the fractional part t = x - floor(x) lies in [1 - 1/n, 1), then f_n(x) = H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: A1 reduces x to t, and L5 computes the value exactly on the top interval.

steps.derives: If the fractional part t = x - floor(x) satisfies t < 1 - 1/n, then m = floor(n*t) cannot be n - 1, so the equality case in L6 is impossible; consequently f_n(x) < H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: From A2, t < 1 - 1/n forces m <= n - 2; then L6 gives g_n(m) < H_n - 1, and A3 transfers this to f_n(t), hence to f_n(x) via A1.

steps.derives: The function x ↦ floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k attains its global maximum H_n - 1 exactly at those real x whose fractional part x - floor(x) lies in [1 - 1/n, 1), equivalently at x = z + t with z an integer and t in [1 - 1/n, 1).
steps.trivial_justification: A5 gives the global upper bound, A6 gives attainment on the top interval, and A7 excludes equality outside that interval; together they identify both the maximal value and the full maximizing set.
